slide.title: ATX-UK Corporation Tax Crash Course
slide.subtitle: Pass-focused revision: understand the map, then practise tomorrow
slide.speakerNotes: Okay, today we are not chasing perfection. We are building the corporation tax map in your head so that tomorrow, when you start questions, you recognise the triggers quickly.

slide.title: What we are covering

bullets.bullet: Rates, augmented profits and associated companies
Capital gains groups, SSE and degrouping
Overseas, R&D, patent box, QIPs and anti-avoidance

slide.speakerNotes: This is the full corporation tax picture. Do not try to memorise it as isolated rules. Think of it as a sequence: compute profits, identify rates, find losses, check groups, then look for special reliefs.

slide.title: The CT machine
slide.speakerNotes: Start with the computation. Bring together all taxable sources, then deduct qualifying charitable donations. The result is taxable total profits. This is the amount on which corporation tax is charged.

slide.title: TTP vs augmented profits

right.heading: Augmented profits
right.point: Used to decide the CT rate and QIP position

slide.examTip: Dividends may be exempt from TTP but still relevant to augmented profits.
slide.speakerNotes: This distinction is vital. Taxable total profits tell us what is taxed. Augmented profits help decide which rate applies. So, if you see dividends, pause. Do not just tax them. Ask whether they affect augmented profits.

slide.title: Corporation tax rates

bullets.bullet: Planning shortcut: marginal band effectively saves 26.5%

slide.warning: Do not apply 26.5% to the whole profit.
slide.speakerNotes: The 26.5% figure is a planning shortcut. It tells us the value of reducing profits in the marginal band. It is not the normal way to calculate the whole corporation tax liability.

slide.title: Associated companies
slide.trigger: Company structure given = check associated companies

bullets.bullet: Limits are divided by associated companies
Short accounting periods also reduce limits
Associated companies affect CT rates and QIPs

slide.speakerNotes: When the exam gives you a group structure, it is rarely decoration. Associated companies can reduce the limits, which can push a company into marginal relief or quarterly instalments.

slide.title: Loss relief overview

row.cell: Current total profits, 12-month carry back, carry forward
Current total profits, 36-month carry back LIFO
Current total profits, prior NTLR profits, future profits

slide.speakerNotes: The first question with any loss is: what type of loss is it? Trading losses, capital losses and loan relationship deficits do not all go to the same place.

slide.title: Trading losses
slide.speakerNotes: Do not automatically carry back. If last year saves tax at 19% but future profits may save 26.5%, future relief may be better. But carry back may give cash earlier. ATX is about advice, not just rules.

slide.title: Terminal losses
slide.memory: Normal loss = 12 months. Terminal loss = 36 months.
slide.speakerNotes: If a company stops trading, your brain should immediately say terminal loss. The key number is 36 months, and the order is latest period first.

slide.title: Three losses students mix up
slide.box: Carry back only against prior NTLR profits
slide.speakerNotes: This slide is important. Capital losses stay in the capital gains box. NTLR deficits have their own carry-back restriction. Trading losses are broader. Keep these separate.

slide.title: Large loss restrictions

bullets.bullet: Brought-forward losses may be restricted where profits are very large
Major ownership change plus major trade change can restrict losses

slide.speakerNotes: For tonight, this is awareness level. If you see very large brought-forward losses or a company being bought with losses, ask whether restrictions could apply.

slide.title: Group relief

bullets.bullet: Capital losses are not ordinary group relief

slide.speakerNotes: Group relief allows losses to move around the group. But be careful: capital losses are not surrendered as ordinary group relief. They belong to the capital gains group rules.

slide.title: Group loss planning order

bullets.bullet: Use losses where they save most tax

slide.speakerNotes: This is one of the most important memory chains. If a group has limited losses, use them first where they save 26.5%, then 25%, then 19%.

slide.title: Group relief is not only tax rate

bullets.bullet: Losses may reduce quarterly instalment payments
Earlier tax relief may be preferable
Do not waste double taxation relief

slide.speakerNotes: A perfect ATX answer considers tax saving and timing. Sometimes a group surrender may be useful because it reduces quarterly payments, not just because it saves more tax overall.

slide.title: Corresponding periods
slide.trigger: Company joins or leaves group mid-year

bullets.bullet: Different year ends may need time apportionment

slide.speakerNotes: If companies were only in the same group for part of the period, do not surrender the full year automatically. Think corresponding accounting period.

slide.title: Consortium relief

bullets.bullet: Several companies jointly own another company
20 or fewer companies together own at least 75%
Each member generally owns at least 5%

slide.speakerNotes: Consortium relief is a trigger topic. If no one company has a 75% group, but several companies together do, think consortium.

slide.title: Capital gains groups

bullets.bullet: Concerned with assets, gains and capital losses
Can support rollover relief and gain/loss elections

slide.speakerNotes: Now switch mental boxes. Group relief is about surrendering losses. Capital gains groups are about assets, gains and capital losses.

slide.title: No gain / no loss transfers

flow.item: Transfers asset to group company B

slide.speakerNotes: Intra-group asset transfers are normally tax neutral for capital gains groups. But remember: the gain has not disappeared. It may come back later through a degrouping charge.

slide.title: Rollover relief in groups

bullets.bullet: One group company sells qualifying business asset
Another group company buys replacement qualifying asset

slide.memory: SSE exempts. Rollover defers. No gain/no loss defers.
slide.speakerNotes: Keep the words clear. Exemption removes tax. Deferral delays tax. Rollover relief is a deferral.

slide.title: Degrouping charge
slide.trigger: Company leaves group while still holding an asset received tax-free

bullets.bullet: Look back for intra-group asset transfers
Old deferred gain may become chargeable

slide.speakerNotes: If a company is sold out of the group, scan the question for an earlier asset transfer. If it received an asset tax-free and still owns it, think degrouping charge.

slide.title: Substantial Shareholding Exemption
slide.trigger: Company sells shares in another company

bullets.bullet: 12 months within the relevant six-year period

slide.warning: Do not use BADR for a company.
slide.speakerNotes: The examiner has warned candidates about missing SSE. Whenever a company sells shares in another company, SSE should be your first thought.

slide.title: SSE + degrouping chain

steps.step: SSE may also exempt the degrouping element

slide.speakerNotes: This chain is exam gold. Do not stop after saying SSE applies. If the company being sold leaves the group, ask whether a degrouping charge also arises.

slide.title: Other gains points

bullets.bullet: Indexation cannot create or increase a loss
Companies do not get the individual annual exempt amount

slide.speakerNotes: This is lower priority than SSE and degrouping, but remember that companies are not individuals. Do not use individual CGT rules blindly.

slide.title: Overseas operations

bullets.bullet: Foreign tax may create double taxation
DTR broadly restricted to UK tax on overseas profits
Do not waste DTR with poor loss planning

slide.speakerNotes: When foreign tax is paid, think double taxation relief. And if losses are available, ask whether using them against overseas profits would waste relief.

slide.title: Branch vs subsidiary

left.heading: Branch
left.point: Useful where early losses may help UK company

right.heading: Subsidiary
right.point: Often attractive once overseas business is profitable

slide.speakerNotes: This is a classic ATX advisory point. Branches can be attractive in early loss-making years. Subsidiaries may become attractive later once profits arise.

slide.title: CFC rules
slide.trigger: Non-UK company controlled from the UK
slide.speakerNotes: Do not overcomplicate CFCs today. Recognise the trigger: non-UK company, UK control, potential low-tax diverted profits.

slide.title: R&D: RDEC
slide.speakerNotes: The simple memory phrase is 20% in, 20% off. Add the RDEC to taxable income, then deduct it from the corporation tax liability.

slide.title: Patent box and full expensing

bullets.bullet: Patent box: qualifying patent profits taxed effectively at 10%
Full expensing: 100% for qualifying new main-rate plant
50% first-year allowance for qualifying new special-rate plant
Cars and second-hand assets do not qualify for full expensing

slide.speakerNotes: R&D rewards innovation spending. Patent box rewards qualifying patent profits. Full expensing accelerates tax relief for qualifying plant and machinery.

slide.title: Corporation tax payments

bullets.bullet: Normal payment: nine months and one day after period end
Return due: 12 months after period end
Large companies may pay quarterly instalments
QIP threshold is affected by associated companies and augmented profits

slide.speakerNotes: Do not only calculate tax. Think about when it is paid. Group relief may improve cash flow if it reduces quarterly instalments.

slide.title: Other company-specific traps

bullets.bullet: Transfer pricing: connected companies must use arm's length prices
Close company loans: possible s455 charge
Close investment-holding companies: main rate only
Personal service companies: employment disguised through a company

slide.speakerNotes: These are trigger topics. You do not need to master every detail tonight, but you must recognise when the scenario is pointing you towards anti-avoidance.

slide.title: The CT exam method

steps.step: Adjust limits for associated companies and short periods
Identify loss type and relief route
Check gains group, SSE and degrouping
Consider overseas, R&D, patent box and QIPs

slide.speakerNotes: This is the answer approach. If you follow this order, you reduce the risk of missing major marks.

slide.title: Final recall triggers
slide.speakerNotes: This is your final memory list. If you can recall these triggers without notes, you are ready to start question practice tomorrow.

slide.title: Tonight’s target
slide.speakerNotes: Do not panic if you cannot recall every exception. For tonight, your win is recognising the main corporation tax triggers. Tomorrow, question practice will turn this into exam technique.
